Other major sectors of the county's economy measured by employment are professional and related services (including education), 14 percent of the workforce; wholesale/ retail trade, 12 percent; and construction, 10 percent.
Table 2-13 indicates that in Oconee County, manufacturing claimed 39 percent of total earnings in 1972. This was followed by government earnings with 24 percent of the total, of which State and local government accounted for 22 percent. The 1972 earnings from the transportation, communication and public utilities sector were 17.49 percent for all earnings.
The Pickens County figures for 1972 contrast somewhat with those of Oconee (Table 2-14). Manufacturing earnings were 59 percent of the total amount of labor's and proprietors' earnings. Government earnings, however, were 9.8 percent of the total, and transportation, communication, and public utilities accounted for only 1.5 percent of the total.
A trend in earnings for the transportation, communication, and public utilities sector of the Oconee County economy has been observed. In 1965 this group accounted for 1.31 percent of all of labor's and proprietors' earnings; by 1972, the figure had risen to 17.49 percent (Table 2-13). This rapid growth is due largely to the construction of the Keowee-Toxaway project begun by Duke Power in 1968. The importance of the Keowee-Toxaway project to the Oconee economy can further be seen in Table 2-15, which shows the location quotient for earnings by broad industrial section. 1/ In 1965 the location quotient for the transportation, communication and public utilities section was .18365; by 1970 this figure had jumped to 2.3680. The location quotient statistics for Pickens County are given in Table 2-16.
If The location quotient measures the relative concentration of an industry in an area. It is computed by expressing earnings in a given industry in an area as a percent of all-industry earnings in the area. This percentage for the area is then divided by the comparable percentage for the Nation, with the resulting ratio termed the location quotient. If the figure is greater than unity, it indicates that the area has an above-average proportion of the industry's output. If the location quotient is less than unity, it indicates that the area is producing a less-than-average amount of that product.
